::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**In plain terms.** This page reports what the pipeline actually *found* — as opposed to
*how* it works, which is threads 1–4. Three blocks: (1) the **measured trap catalog** (how deep
the traps sit, how strongly they capture, how long they hold charge), (2) the **completeness bound**
and the hidden-population it implies, and (3) the **simulation's bottom line** for the SENSEI
single-electron dark-matter background.

The headline is **two numbers**: the *measured/characterized* trap impact on the masked
single-electron rate is **null**; the residual risk is an **efficiency-corrected 90% CL upper
limit** on a hidden long-τ population, reported with an error band rather than floored.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Campaign numbers will be superseded.** The V1/V3 phase-split kernel fix (physics [§2.4](physics.qmd),
[§6](physics.qmd)) supersedes the pre-split campaign numbers; the production rerun at
`v3_phase_fraction = 0.5` is in progress. The **catalog** and **completeness** figures below are
current. The **campaign** figures in §4 are the *current* (pre-split) simulation — shown to
illustrate the shape of the result — and will be regenerated when the rerun lands (tracked in
`NOTEBOOK_COMPLETION_TODO.md`, item 1). The A/B test redistributes excess from slope to intercept, so
expect the §4 numbers to shift, not the qualitative null-vs-allowance story.
:::

## 1. The headline

The headline is **two numbers**, both conditional on hidden traps sharing the *observed* E/σ
distribution and — for the upper limit — the *observed* brightness distribution (the conditionality
is spelled out in §6):

- **Measured / characterized (the null).** The ~3,798 characterized traps (the real, decoy-rejected
  population) perturb the masked single-electron rate by an amount consistent with **zero** — the
  simulated masked excess for the baseline population equals the no-trap truth (physics
  [§4.4](physics.qmd)).
- **Efficiency-corrected 90% CL upper limit (the allowance).** Inflating the characterized
  population by the per-bin completeness `1/ε` and taking the 90% CL gives an upper *allowance* for a
  hidden long-τ population — an exposure-dependent masked-rate slope of order **2.8 × 10⁻⁶**
  (pre-rerun value). Its statistical error is **~±22% on the trap-driven excess** (Poisson √20/20 on
  the ~20 anchoring long-τ detections; the excess is the ~+1.0 × 10⁻⁶ above the ~1.8 × 10⁻⁶ no-trap
  truth, so this is ~±8% on the quoted total — and a floor, since the 1/ε weighting makes the
  effective count somewhat below 20). That is the only computed error — an earlier "~25% band incl.
  completeness systematic" phrasing described a band that was never built (audit 2026-07-06). The allowance is additionally
  **conditional on the amplitude prior**: ε assumes hidden traps share the *detected* traps'
  brightness, and the Stage-05 prior is faint-end-truncated by selection. The cached stress variants
  quantify the conditionality — if hidden traps were 2× (4×) fainter, `1/ε` in the UL driver band
  τ ∈ [3×10⁵, 5×10⁷] s grows **×1.4–2.8** (**×2.7–9.3**) (completeness
  [§8](completeness_efficiency.qmd)); this is stated as a condition on the headline, not folded into
  an error band. The allowance is **not floored**: ~21 characterized, decoy-rejected traps at
  τ > 10⁶ s are real evidence the region is populated, so an ε-floor would assert the null by fiat.

The rest of the page is the evidence for each.

## 2. The measured trap catalog

The production (minimal, calibrated-detection) catalog characterizes **~3,798 traps** across the four
quadrants — those that pass the finder, have ≥4 good-temperature intensity fits, are
orientation-consistent, and yield a good Arrhenius energy fit (the funnel in §2.4). Each carries a
fitted depth `E`, capture cross-section `σ`, and per-temperature emission times `τ(T)`.

## 3. Completeness and the upper-limit population

per-τ135 recoverable fraction `ε(τ135)`; dividing the census by it produces the

## 4. Simulation campaign results

`run_campaign.py` runs the catalog and the upper-limit population through the CCD readout simulation
across a scenario grid and reports the **masked single-electron rate** (trap vs no-trap, after the
`hotcol.py`-faithful masking) as a linear fit in exposure time: an exposure-**independent** intercept
(per-image / prompt) and an exposure-**dependent** slope (per-day / deferred). All figures below are
the **current** campaign (minimal_caldet, central V_p = 3 µm³, shuffled order, `post_readout` spurious
charge) — they will be **superseded** by the `v3_phase_fraction = 0.5` rerun but show the shape of the
result. On `post_readout`: it adds the identical spurious-charge realization to both branches *after*
readout, preserving a clean common-random-number cancellation — at the cost that spurious charge never
traverses the traps, i.e. deviation-budget term B (readout capture of spurious 1e) is absent from
these runs ([physics](physics.qmd) §4.2, §6.2; `pre_readout` is the single-run code default).

### 4.3 Where the upper-limit slope lives (τ-band)

Capping the upper-limit seed at successive τ_max and re-running isolates *which* traps carry the
exposure-dependent excess (physics [§4.4](physics.qmd)). Pre-phase-split values, to be refreshed:

| seed τ_max | N traps | slope (exp-dep) | intercept (exp-indep) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 10⁵ | 4,179 | 1.84×10⁻⁶ (≈ no-trap truth) | 9.9×10⁻⁵ |
| 10⁶ | 5,529 | 2.11×10⁻⁶ | 1.01×10⁻⁴ |
| 5×10⁷ (prod cap) | 17,475 | 2.82×10⁻⁶ | 9.96×10⁻⁵ |
| **baseline (characterized)** | **3,798** | **1.82×10⁻⁶ (= truth)** | **9.9×10⁻⁵ (= truth)** |

: The slope band is τ > 10⁵ s (days–months), dominated by τ ∈ [10⁶, 5×10⁷]; it **converges** in
τ_max (the production 5×10⁷ cap sits past the turnover). The baseline is the truth (null); the UL
slope is the 1/ε-inflation headroom, not a measured effect. {tbl-colwidths="[24,16,30,30]"}

## 5. Systematics ledger

One place for every knob and assumption behind the numbers above.

| systematic | how carried | size / direction | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Packet volume V_p** | 1–10 µm³ band (baseline 3), campaign axis | mild on upper via α ∝ 1/V; negligible on baseline | quoted as a band |
| **σ (cross-section)** | folds into V_p (σ/V_p degenerate) | absorbed; no separate term | closed |
| **½ phase fraction** (`v3_phase_fraction`) | knob, bracket by running 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 | controls slope↔intercept split (A/B: intercept +45%, slope −3.2%) | not a big deal; bounded |
| **Phase-blindness ×1.5** | *not applied* | would inflate UL, but V2 traps behave differently (charge is held there) — inflation is not physically correct | **rejected** |
| **High-T Arrhenius lean** | bracket: hot points as-measured (A) vs un-leaned (B), live energy-fit refit ([signed_refit](signed_refit.qmd) §6b) | **≤7%** on the UL-slope driver band (30 → 28 traps), **0%** on the τ135 > 1 hr tail fraction — far below the V_p band. Mechanism identified by shape: thermally activated capture, E_b ≈ 0.16 eV; instrumental cause excluded | settled 2026-07-03; third-variant check (2026-07-06) **confirms production is the conservative end**: taking the activated mechanism as true moves hot-only τ135 *down* (median −0.21 dex), tail identical (1.47%) under A/B/C, driver band 30/28/26 |
| **Amplitude prior / P_c(T)** | Method-3 Stage 05/10; faint-by-2/4 cached | **one-sided up**, and much larger in the UL driver band than at the plateau: mean completeness @10³ s drops 0.992 → 0.920 → 0.744, but at τ = 10⁵/10⁶/10⁷ s the faint-by-2 (faint-by-4) variants inflate `1/ε` by **×1.4–2.8** (**×2.7–9.3**); falling P_c(T) at high T is *real* incompleteness | **resolved by disposition (2026-07-06, TODO 5.2)**: the "~25% band" was audit-traced to a never-computed recommendation (Poisson 1/√20 alone); headline now quotes ±22% Poisson as the statistical error and carries the faint-prior axis as an **explicit conditionality** (hidden traps assumed as bright as detected ones), with the driver-band stress numbers stated, not folded |
| **High-energy-event (HEE) model** | clusters from **one** 20 h MINOS image, deterministically scaled with exposure; SNOLAB = same library ÷10 ([physics](physics.qmd) §7) | trap occupancy — and hence the trap-effect **scale** — tracks the HEE rate, so this is plausibly the dominant scale uncertainty on the allowance; the suppressed event-count variance also makes the run-to-run spread (and any UL-slope significance) optimistic | named scale systematic; Poisson-bootstrap sampler itself stays a deferred implementation |
| **Masking fidelity** | `hotcol.py`-faithful; sim masks slightly stricter than real | quoted masked excess errs **low** | documented |

---

## 6. What is — and isn't — claimed

**Claimed.** Assuming hidden traps share the *observed* E/σ distribution **and the observed
brightness (the Stage-05 amplitude prior)**: the measured/characterized trap impact on the masked
single-electron rate is null, and the hidden long-τ population is bounded by the
efficiency-corrected 90% CL upper limit above (statistical error ~±22% on the trap-driven excess
over the no-trap truth slope, Poisson on the anchoring detections; ~±8% on the quoted total). The amplitude condition is load-bearing: the prior is selection-truncated at the faint
end, and a hidden population 2× (4×) fainter than anything characterized would inflate the
driver-band `1/ε` by ×1.4–2.8 (×2.7–9.3) — see §1 and completeness
[§8](completeness_efficiency.qmd).

**Not claimed / genuinely unbounded.**

- A trap sitting outside the measurable band at *every* temperature is invisible and unbounded by any
  of these methods (needs an independent handle: colder measurement, longer t_ph, or a
  dark-current/leakage argument).
- A population hiding at an E/σ the protocol rarely characterizes is not bounded.
- The upper-limit slope is an *allowance*, not a detection; the baseline is null.

**Open (this page).**

- Campaign numbers (§4) pending the `v3_phase_fraction = 0.5` rerun.
- Survivor-free P_c re-measurement (thread 3, §9) would fully de-bias the genuine-fading fraction.
